At December&#160;31, 2013, Oneida Financial Corp. had consolidated assets of $742.5 million, total deposits of $637.2 million, and stockholders&#8217; equity of $90.7 million.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Oneida Financial Corp.&#8217;s executive offices are located at 182 Main Street, Oneida, New York 13421.&#160; Its telephone number at this address is (315) 363-2000 and its website address is www.oneidafinancial.com.&#160; Information on this website is not and should not be considered to be a part of this annual report and Form&#160;10-K.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Oneida Savings Bank</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Oneida Savings Bank is a New York chartered savings bank headquartered in Oneida, New York.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank was originally founded in 1866 as a mutual (meaning no stockholders) savings bank.&#160; In 1998, Oneida Savings Bank converted to a New York chartered stock savings bank and reorganized from the mutual to the two-tiered mutual holding company form of organization.&#160; In 2010, Oneida Financial Corp. completed its conversion from the mutual holding company structure to stock ownership.  Since 1998 the Bank has grown its traditional community banking franchise organically and through acquisitions of banks and nonbank companies that offer insurance sales, financial services, employee benefits consulting and other risk management products and services. The expansion into insurance and other financial services businesses has enabled Oneida Savings Bank to evolve from a traditional savings bank to a full-service financial services organization.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Oneida Savings Bank&#8217;s deposits are insured by the FDIC up to the maximum amount permitted by law.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank is a community bank engaged primarily in the business of accepting deposits from customers through its main office and 10 full service branch offices and using those deposits, together with funds generated from operations and borrowings to make one-to-four family residential and commercial real estate loans, consumer loans and commercial business loans and to invest in mortgage-backed and other securities.&#160; Municipal deposit banking services are provided through a limited purpose commercial bank subsidiary, The State Bank of Chittenango.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank also sells insurance and other commercial services and products, provides employee benefit services and offers risk management services to help mitigate and prevent work related injuries through Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates,&#160;Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary, and provides financial and investment advisory services through Oneida Wealth Management Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank is subject to comprehensive regulation and examination by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and the New York State Department of Financial Services.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">The State Bank of Chittenango</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The State Bank of Chittenango is a New York chartered limited purpose commercial bank headquartered in Chittenango, New York.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank acquired State Bank of Chittenango in 2002 and retained the municipal banking operations of State Bank of Chittenango in a limited purpose wholly owned subsidiary.&#160; New York State law prohibits a savings bank from directly soliciting and servicing public funds (deposits of counties, cities, towns, school districts,&#160;etc.).&#160; Holding State Bank of Chittenango as a limited purpose commercial bank subsidiary has enabled us to offer municipal deposit banking services throughout our market area.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, State Bank of Chittenango held $185.0 million in assets, consisting primarily of U.S. Government obligations, mortgage-backed securities and tax exempt securities.&#160; The investment securities maintained at State Bank of Chittenango are used to collateralize $145.4 million in municipal deposits. All disclosures in this annual report and Form&#160;10-K relating to Oneida Financial Corp.&#8217;s investments and deposits include the investments and deposits that are held by State Bank of Chittenango.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates,&#160;Inc. is the wholly owned insurance agency, risk management and employee benefit subsidiary of Oneida Savings Bank and is headquartered in Oneida, New York. It has six other offices in New York State and one office in South Carolina.  Oneida Savings Bank completed the acquisition of Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates in 2000. Bailey&#160;&amp; </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">1</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s6101595da46c40e498ab9cdd44777a1f"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Haskell Associates is a full-service insurance, risk management and employee benefits firm with over 130 employees providing services to over 19,000 customers.&#160; Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates offers personal and commercial property insurance and other risk management products and services.&#160; In addition, Bailey &amp; Haskell Associates offers employee benefit related services.  Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates represents many leading insurance companies, including Travelers, CNA, Hartford, Progressive, Cincinnati and Utica National. We have acquired seven insurance agencies in the years following the acquisition of Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates, including Schenectady Insuring Agency,&#160;Inc. which was added during 2012. All of the acquired insurance agencies were merged into Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates.&#160; </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The risk management services provided by Bailey &amp; Haskell Associates were those previously provided through the wholly owned risk management subsidiary Workplace Health Solutions.  Workplace Health Solutions was established in January&#160;2008 as a risk management company with services to help mitigate and prevent work related injuries.&#160; Specifically, Workplace Health Solutions works with employers to develop informed hiring programs, coordinates employee training programs and consults with and advises employers relative to workers&#8217; compensation coverage and incidents.&#160; In addition, this subsidiary develops a network of medical professionals to evaluate injured workers and arrange for proper treatment of and recovery from workplace injuries from a risk management perspective.&#160; Workplace Health Solutions was developed to complement and refer the products and services offered by our other subsidiaries with an overall philosophy of providing innovative risk management services.&#160; Effective January 1, 2013, Workplace Health Solutions was merged with Bailey &amp; Haskell Associates to better align services provided to customers. The combination of acquired agencies and organic growth has resulted in total revenue for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 of $19.7 million, an increase of 11.9% or $2.1 million, from $17.6 million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2012.  All disclosures in this annual report and Form&#160;10-K relating to Oneida Financial Corp. are consolidated to include the activities of Bailey&#160;&amp; Haskell Associates.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Oneida Wealth Management</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Benefit Consulting Group,&#160;Inc., originally acquired in 2006, was the wholly owned employee benefits consulting and retirement plan administration subsidiary of Oneida Savings Bank.&#160; Effective January 1, 2013, the subsidiary was reorganized to better align services provided to customers. 2012.&#160; All disclosures in this annual report and Form&#160;10-K relating to Oneida Financial Corp. are consolidated to include the activities of Oneida Wealth Management.</font></div><div credit unions, finance companies, mutual funds, insurance companies, and brokerage and investment banking firms operating locally and elsewhere.&#160; Many of these competitors have substantially greater resources and lending limits than we do and may offer certain services that we do not or cannot provide.&#160; Moreover, credit unions which offer substantially the same services as we offer are not subject to federal or state income taxation.&#160; Trends toward consolidation of the financial services industry and the removal of restrictions on interstate branching and banking powers may make it more difficult for smaller institutions such as Oneida Savings Bank to compete effectively with large national and regional banking institutions.&#160; Our profitability depends upon the ability to successfully compete in our market area.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:10pt;"><font have originated adjustable-rate mortgage (&#8220;ARM&#8221;) loans for retention in our portfolio.&#160;&#160; As a result of the continuation of relatively low market interest rates in recent periods, borrowers have shown a preference for fixed-rate loans.&#160; Consequently, in recent periods we have originated more fixed-rate one-to-four family loans.&#160; We generally sell our fixed-rate one-to-four family loan originations with maturities exceeding fifteen years and such loans are sold without recourse and on a servicing retained basis.&#160; In order to complement our traditional emphasis of one-to-four family residential real estate lending, management has sought to increase the number of higher yielding commercial real estate loans, consumer loans and commercial business loans.&#160; To a limited extent, we will originate loans secured by multi-family properties.</font></div><div Fixed-rate loans are originated for terms of up to 30 years.&#160; One-to-four family fixed-rate loans are offered with a monthly payment feature.&#160; We do not originate and have not originated sub-prime, Alt-A, negative amortization or other higher risk residential mortgage loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">We originate both adjustable-rate and fixed-rate one-to-four family loans.&#160; As a result of the continued low interest rate environment during the past year, a greater percentage of our one-to-four family loan originations consisted of fixed-rate one-to-four family mortgage loans.&#160; Our practice in recent years has been to sell in the secondary market substantially all of our fixed-rate one-to-four family loan originations with maturities exceeding fifteen years on a servicing retained basis without recourse to Oneida Savings Bank.&#160; Currently, we have no intention of changing our practice of selling our fixed-rate loan originations, although we may determine to change this practice in the future.&#160; In a rising interest rate environment, we expect that a greater percentage of our loan originations will consist of adjustable-rate loans, which we generally retain in our portfolio.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, loans serviced by Oneida Savings Bank for others totaled $107.8 million.&#160; During the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and December&#160;31, 2012, we sold $12.4 million and $22.9 million, respectively, in fixed-rate one-to-four family loans.&#160; As of December&#160;31, 2013, we had $1.8 million of mortgage loan forward sale commitments.&#160; The fair value of these commitments is not material.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The interest rate on ARM loans is indexed to the one year Treasury bill rate.&#160; Our ARM loans currently provide for maximum rate adjustments of 200 basis points per year and either 500 or 600 basis points over the term of the loan depending on the length of the adjustable portion of the loan.&#160; In the current rate environment the fully indexed equivalent loan rate is less than the initial interest rate on the ARM loans. Residential ARM loans amortize over a maximum term of up to 30 years.&#160; In addition to one year ARM loans, we offer certain hybrid ARM loans which provide for an initial fixed term of three or five years and then are converted into a one year ARM loan after the fixed time period. ARM loans are originated for retention in our portfolio.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">ARM loans decrease the risk associated with changes in market interest rates by periodically repricing, but involve other risks.&#160; As interest rates increase, the underlying required periodic payments by the borrower increase, thus increasing the potential for default by the borrower. At the same time, the marketability of the underlying collateral may be adversely affected by higher interest rates. Upward adjustment of the contractual interest rate is also limited by the maximum periodic and lifetime interest rate adjustment permitted by the terms of the ARM loans, and therefore, is potentially limited in effectiveness during periods of rapidly rising interest rates.&#160; Decreasing interest rates could result in a downward adjustment of the contractual interest rates resulting in lower interest income. At December&#160;31, 2013, $52.0 million, or 15.4% of our loan portfolio consisted of one-to-four family residential loans with adjustable interest rates.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">All one-to-four family residential mortgage loans originated by Oneida Savings Bank include &#8220;due-on-sale&#8221; clauses, which give us the right to declare a loan immediately due and payable in the event that, among other things, the borrower sells or otherwise disposes of the real property subject to the mortgage and the loan is not repaid.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At December&#160;31, 2013, approximately $117.4 million, or 34.7% of our loan portfolio, consisted of one-to-four family residential loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Home Equity Loans.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; We offer home equity loans that are secured by the borrower&#8217;s primary residence.&#160; We offer a home equity line of credit under which the borrower is permitted to draw on the home equity line of credit during the first ten years after it is originated and repay the outstanding balance over a term not to exceed 25 years from the date the line of credit is originated.&#160; The interest rates on home equity lines of credit adjust monthly  a margin over the prime interest rate.&#160; We also offer a home equity product providing for a fixed-rate of interest.&#160; Both adjustable-rate and fixed-rate home equity loans are underwritten under the same criteria that we use to underwrite one-to-four family fixed-rate loans.&#160; Fixed-rate home equity loans are originated with terms up to fifteen years.&#160; Home equity loans may be underwritten with a loan to value ratio of 90% when combined with the principal balance of the existing mortgage loan.&#160; The maximum amount of a home equity loan may not exceed $1.0 million unless approved by the Board of Directors.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;We generally require an appraisal on the property securing loans in excess of $75,000 at the time of the loan application (but not thereafter) in order to determine the value of the property securing the home equity loans.&#160; We utilize alternative methods in determining the value of properties of loans less than $75,000 such as a limited appraisal or review of tax bills.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, the outstanding balance of home equity loans totaled $49.4 million, or 14.7% of our loan portfolio.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commercial Real Estate Loans.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;At December&#160;31, 2013, $82.4 million, or 24.4% of the total loan portfolio consisted of commercial real estate and multi-family loans.&#160; Commercial real estate and multi-family residential loans are secured by office buildings, medical facilities, mixed-use properties, religious facilities, other commercial properties and multi-family residential </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">6</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s92c6e73155ff4737a8d04dd282f44f1e"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">properties. We originate adjustable rate commercial mortgage loans with terms of up to 20 years.&#160; The maximum loan-to-value ratio of commercial real estate loans is 80%.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, the largest commercial real estate loan had a principal balance of $3.0 million and was secured by an office building and fixtures.&#160;&#160; This loan was performing in accordance with its terms at December&#160;31, 2013.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">In underwriting commercial real estate and multi-family residential loans, we review the expected net operating income generated by the real estate to ensure that it is at least 110% of the amount of the monthly debt service; the age and condition of the collateral; the financial resources and income level of the borrower; and the borrower&#8217;s business experience.&#160; Personal guarantees are routinely obtained from all commercial real estate borrowers.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Loans secured by commercial real estate and multi-family residential properties generally are larger than one-to-four family residential loans and involve a greater degree of risk. Commercial and multi-family residential mortgage loans often involve large loan balances to single borrowers or groups of related borrowers. Payments on these loans depend to a large degree on the results of operations and management of the properties or underlying businesses, and may be affected to a greater extent by adverse conditions in the real estate market or the economy in general. Accordingly, the nature of commercial real estate loans makes them more difficult for management to monitor and evaluate.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Construction and Land.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, construction and land loans totaled $8.9 million, or 2.6% of the total loan portfolio.&#160; We generally do not originate speculative construction loans, and we had no such loans in our portfolio at December&#160;31, 2013.  Our construction and land loans consisted of $1.1 million of fixed-rate one-to-four family residential construction loans as well as $7.8 million of commercial new construction loans.&#160; One-to-four family residential construction loans are offered as interest-only loans at a fixed rate of interest for up to a five month construction period.&#160; Immediately following the construction period the loan begins monthly amortizing payments consistent with the terms of the one-to-four family permanent mortgage loan product.&#160; Commercial construction loans can consist of land development loans or new building construction loans as well as participation loans that include new building construction loans.&#160; Land development loans are collateralized by a mortgage on the property which is supported by an appraisal.&#160; Commercial construction loans are given for the construction phase of a building.&#160; There can be an interest only period not exceeding one year for new construction loans. Once the construction is completed, the loan is transferred into permanent financing.&#160; Draws for both residential and commercial new construction are based on the loan approval, commitment letter, and a building and loan agreement.&#160; Property inspections during the construction phase are also required.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Construction financing generally involves greater credit risk than long-term financing on improved, owner-occupied real estate.&#160; Risk of loss on a construction loan depends largely upon the accuracy of the initial estimate of the value of the property at completion of construction compared to the estimated cost (including interest) of construction and other assumptions.&#160; If the estimate of construction cost proves to be inaccurate, we may be required to advance additional funds beyond the amount originally committed in order to protect the value of the property.&#160; Moreover, if the estimated value of the completed project proves to be inaccurate, the borrower may hold a property with a value that is insufficient to assure full repayment of the construction loan upon the sale of the property.&#160; In the event we make a land acquisition loan on property that is not yet approved for the planned development, there is the risk that approvals will not be granted or will be delayed.&#160; Construction loans also expose us to the risk that improvements will not be completed on time in accordance with specifications and projected costs.&#160; In addition, the ultimate sale or rental of the property may not occur as anticipated.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Consumer Lending</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, consumer loans totaled $28.8 million, or 8.5% of the total loan portfolio.&#160; Our consumer loans consist primarily of automobile loans, and to a lesser extent recreational vehicle loans, secured personal loans (secured by bonds, equity securities or other readily marketable collateral), and other consumer loans (consisting of passbook loans and unsecured home improvement loans).&#160; Consumer loans are originated with terms to maturity of three to seven years.&#160; Historically, we have sought to increase the level of consumer loans primarily through increased automobile lending.&#160;&#160; We participate in a number of indirect automobile lending programs with local automobile dealerships.&#160; All indirect automobile loans must satisfy our underwriting criteria for automobile loans originated directly by us to the borrower and must be approved by one of our lending officers.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, loans secured by automobiles totaled $25.8 million, of which $15.9 million were originated through our indirect automobile lending program.&#160;&#160; We have also sought to increase the level of automobile loans directly to borrowers by increasing marketing efforts with existing customers.&#160; Automobile loans generally do not have terms exceeding seven years.&#160; We do not provide financing for leased automobiles.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Consumer loans generally have shorter terms and higher interest rates than one-to-four family mortgage loans. In addition, consumer loans expand the products and services we offer to better meet the financial services needs of our customers.&#160; Consumer loans generally involve greater credit risk than residential mortgage loans because of the difference in the underlying collateral.&#160; Repossessed collateral for a defaulted consumer loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment of the outstanding loan balance because of the greater likelihood of damage to, loss of, or depreciation in the underlying collateral.  The remaining </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">7</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s92c6e73155ff4737a8d04dd282f44f1e"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">deficiency often does not warrant further substantial collection efforts against the borrower beyond obtaining a deficiency judgment. In addition, consumer loan collections depend on the borrower&#8217;s personal financial stability.&#160; Furthermore, the application of various federal and state laws, including federal and state bankruptcy and insolvency laws, may limit the amount that can be recovered on such loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our underwriting procedures for consumer loans include an assessment of the applicant&#8217;s credit history and the ability to meet existing and proposed debt obligations. Although the applicant&#8217;s creditworthiness is the primary consideration, the underwriting process also includes a comparison of the value of the security to the proposed loan amount. We underwrite consumer loans internally, which we believe limits its exposure to credit risks associated with loans underwritten or purchased from brokers and other external sources.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Commercial Business Loans.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, we had $50.9 million of commercial business loans which represented 15.1% of the total loan portfolio.&#160; Commercial business loans are originated with terms of up to ten years, at fixed rates of interest except for lines of credit which have variable rates of interest.&#160; Commercial business loans are generally originated to persons with a prior relationship with Oneida Savings Bank or referrals from persons with a prior relationship with Oneida Savings Bank. The decision to grant a commercial business loan depends primarily on the creditworthiness and cash flow of the borrower (and any guarantors) and secondarily on the value of and ability to liquidate the collateral which generally consists of receivables, inventory and equipment.&#160; We generally require annual financial statements and tax returns from our commercial business borrowers and personal guarantees from the commercial business borrowers.&#160; We also generally require an appraisal of any real estate that secures the commercial business loan.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, the largest commercial business loan totaled $2.2 million, which was secured by business assets, life insurance and liquid collateral of a for-profit telecom provider. At December&#160;31, 2013, unsecured commercial business loans totaled $814,000.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Commercial business lending generally involves greater risk than residential mortgage lending and involves risks that are different from those associated with residential and commercial real estate lending. Real estate lending is generally considered to be collateral based, with loan amounts based on predetermined loan to collateral values and liquidation of the underlying real estate collateral is viewed as the primary source of repayment in the event of borrower default. Although commercial business loans may be collateralized by equipment or other business assets, the liquidation of collateral in the event of a borrower default is often an insufficient source of repayment because equipment and other business assets may be obsolete or of limited use, among other things. Accordingly, the repayment of a commercial business loan depends primarily on the creditworthiness of the borrower (and any guarantors), while liquidation of collateral is a secondary source of repayment.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:12px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><a name="sd927fe0442f54efda0bcc6c90880e50c"></a><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Maturity Schedule.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">&#160;</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#32;The following table sets forth certain information as of December&#160;31, 2013, regarding the amount of loans (including loans held for sale) maturing in our portfolio.&#160; Demand loans having no stated schedule of repayment and no stated maturity and overdrafts are reported as due in one year or less.&#160; All loans are included in the period in which the final contractual repayment is due.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Approval Procedures and Authority.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; The Board of Directors establishes our lending policies and loan approval limits.&#160; Loan officers generally have the authority to originate mortgage loans, consumer loans and commercial business loans up to amounts established for each lending officer.&#160; All residential loans over $500,000 must be approved by the Officer Loan Committee. The Officer Loan Committee shall consist of at least three members with at least one member being the President, Chief Executive Officer or Chief Loan Officer present to vote.  The Officer Loan Committee consists of the President, the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Loan Officer, and the Managed Assets Department Head or a Designated Bank Officer.&#160; All loan relationships in excess of $500,000 and up to $2.0 million (exclusive of residential mortgages and home equity loans secured by a lien on the borrower&#8217;s primary residence) must be approved by the Officer Loan Committee.&#160; All lending relationships in excess of $2.0 million up to $4.0 million (exclusive of residential mortgages and home equity loans secured by a lien on the borrower&#8217;s primary residence) must be approved by the Executive Committee of the Board of Directors.&#160; All lending relationships in excess of $4.0 million must be approved by the Board of Directors.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">All independent appraisers are approved by the Board of Directors annually.&#160; We require an environmental site assessment for all non-residential mortgage loans.&#160; Our policy is to require hazard insurance on all mortgage loans and generally to require title insurance on all residential mortgage loans.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loan Origination Fees and Other Income</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; In addition to interest earned on loans, we receive loan origination fees.&#160; Such fees and costs vary with the volume and type of loans and commitments made and purchased, principal repayments and competitive conditions in the mortgage markets, which in turn respond to the demand and availability of money.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">10</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">In addition to loan origination fees, we also receive other fees, servicing income and other income that consist primarily of mortgage servicing fees and late charges.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loans-to-One Borrower</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.&#160; Savings banks are subject to the same loans-to-one borrower limits as those applicable to national banks, which under current regulations restrict loans-to-one borrower to an amount equal to 15% of unimpaired net worth on an unsecured basis, and an additional 10% of unimpaired net worth in the case of loans that are fully secured by readily marketable collateral having a market value, as determined by reliable and continuously available price quotations at least equal to the amount of the loan.&#160; Our policy provides that loans-to-one borrower (or related borrowers) should not exceed 15% of our capital.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At December&#160;31, 2013, the largest amount loaned to one borrower consisted of seven commercial real estate loans and five commercial loans with an outstanding balance totaling $4.7 million and available credit of $3.3 million.&#160; This amount was secured by commercial property including multiple office buildings and business assets as well as various one-to-four family and farm properties. The loans also carry personal guarantees.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013 this lending relationship was performing in accordance with its terms.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Asset Quality, Delinquencies and Classified Assets</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Collection Procedures.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; A computer generated late notice is sent when a loan&#8217;s grace period ends.&#160; After the late notice has been mailed, accounts are assigned to collectors for follow-up to determine reasons for delinquency and explore payment options.&#160; Generally, loans that are 30 days delinquent will receive a default notice.&#160; With respect to consumer loans, we will commence efforts to repossess the collateral after the loan becomes 45 days delinquent.&#160; Loans secured by real estate that are delinquent over 60 days are turned over to our Managed Asset Manager.&#160; Generally, after 90 days we will commence legal action.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Loans Past Due and Nonperforming Assets</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; Loans are reviewed on a regular basis and are placed on non-accrual status when they are 90 days past due or earlier when, in the opinion of management, the collection of additional interest is doubtful.&#160; Loans are generally placed on non-accrual status when either principal or interest is 90 days or more past due.&#160; Interest accrued and unpaid at the time a loan is placed on non-accrual status is reversed from interest income.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Real estate acquired as a result of foreclosure or by deed in lieu of foreclosure is classified as Other Real Estate (&#8220;ORE&#8221;) until such time as it is sold.&#160; When real estate is acquired through foreclosure or by deed in lieu of foreclosure, it is recorded at its fair value, less estimated costs of disposal.&#160; If the value of the property is less than the loan balance, less any related specific loan loss provisions, the difference is charged against the allowance for loan losses.&#160; Any subsequent write-down of ORE is charged against earnings.</font></div><div December&#160;31, 2013, our classified assets included loans identified by bank regulatory definitions of &#8220;substandard&#8221;.&#160; We had no assets classified as &#8220;doubtful&#8221; at December&#160;31, 2013 that were not also considered impaired and included in the impaired assets total.&#160; We had no assets classified as &#8220;loss&#8221; at December&#160;31, 2013.&#160; Substandard assets consisted of (i)&#160;four commercial relationships with a principal balance of $1.4 million, (ii)&#160;two one-to-four family residential loans with a principal balance of $218,000, and (iii)&#160;three home equity loans with a principal balance of $262,000.&#160; In addition to the classified assets, we have identified certain impaired assets at December&#160;31, 2013 consisting of (i)&#160;three commercial real estate loans with a principal balance of $504,000 and (ii)&#160;six commercial loans with a principal balance of $925,000.  Included as a component of criticized assets are loans identified as &#8220;special mention&#8221; as determined by management according to regulatory guidance.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, we did not have any loans identified as special mention.  In addition, we have a classified other asset totaling $2.0 million which represents surplus notes to an insurance company specializing in professional liability for medical malpractice.  This asset is considered classified based on changes in management at the insurance company and the loss taken during 2012 related to a similar investment in an insurance company specializing in long-term care facilities.  These surplus notes were performing as of December 31, 2013.  We no not anticipate a loss on these notes.   </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Allowance for Loan Losses</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; The allowance for loan losses is a valuation allowance for probable incurred credit losses. Loan losses are charged against the allowance when management believes the uncollectibility of a loan balance is confirmed. Subsequent recoveries, if any, are credited to the allowance.&#160; Management estimates the allowance balance required using past loan loss experience, the nature and volume of the portfolio, information about specific borrower situations and estimated collateral values, economic conditions, and other factors.&#160; Allocations of the allowance may be made for specific loans, but the entire allowance is available for any loan that, in management&#8217;s judgment, should be charged off.&#160;&#160; The allowance consists of specific and general components.&#160; The specific component relates to loans that are individually classified as impaired.&#160; The general component covers non-impaired loans and is based on the historical loss experience adjusted for current factors.&#160; The historical loss experience is determined by portfolio segment and is based on the actual loss history experienced by the Company over the most recent three years.&#160; This actual loss experience is supplemented with other economic factors based on the risks present for each portfolio segment.&#160; These economic factors include consideration of the following:&#160; levels of and trends in delinquencies and impaired loans; levels of and trends in charge-offs and recoveries; trends in volume and terms of loans; effects of any changes in risk selection and underwriting standards; other changes in lending policies, procedures, and practices; experience, ability and depth of lending management and other relevant staff; national and local economic trends and conditions; industry conditions; and effects of changes in credit concentrations.&#160; Management makes appropriate provisions for loan losses on a quarterly basis.&#160; In addition, various regulatory agencies, as an integral part of their examination process, periodically review our allowance for loan losses and valuation of real estate owned.&#160; Such agencies may require us to recognize additions to the allowance based on their judgment about information available to them at the time of their examination.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, the total allowance was $3.1 million, which amounted to 0.93% of loans, net and 587.9% of nonperforming loans.&#160;&#160; For the years ended December&#160;31, 2013 and 2012, we had net charge-offs of $166,000 and $864,000, respectively, against this allowance.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">15</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s47e41702b5fd419890fc472c7a70ad17"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Securities Investment Activities</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The securities investment policy is established by our Board of Directors.&#160; This policy dictates that investment decisions will be made based on the safety of the investment, our liquidity needs, potential returns, cash flow targets and desired risk parameters.&#160; In pursuing these objectives, management considers the ability of an investment to provide earnings consistent with factors of quality, maturity, marketability, liquidity and risk diversification.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Our current policies generally limit security investments to U.S. Government and agency securities, tax-exempt bonds, public utilities debt obligations, corporate debt obligations and corporate equity securities. In addition, our policy permits investments in mortgage related securities, including securities issued by government sponsored enterprises such as Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae.&#160;&#160; Our investment strategy is to increase overall investment securities yields while managing interest rate risk.&#160; We will only purchase securities rated as investment grade by a nationally recognized investment rating agency.&#160; We do not engage in any hedging transactions, such as interest rate swaps or caps.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">We evaluate securities for other-than-temporary impairment (&#8220;OTTI&#8221;) on at least a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market conditions warrant such an evaluation.&#160; For securities in an unrealized loss position, management considers the extent and duration of the unrealized loss, and the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer.&#160; Management also assesses whether it intends to sell, or it is more likely than not that it will be required to sell, a security in an unrealized loss position before recovery of its amortized cost basis.&#160; If either of the criteria regarding intent or requirement to sell is met, the entire difference between amortized cost and fair value is recognized as impairment through earnings.&#160; For debt securities that do not meet the aforementioned criteria, the amount of impairment is split into two components as follows:&#160; 1) OTTI related to credit loss, which must be recognized in the income statement and 2) OTTI related to other factors, which is recognized in other comprehensive income.&#160; The credit loss is defined as the difference between the present value of the cash flows expected to be collected and the amortized cost basis.&#160; The assessment of whether an other-than-temporary impairment decline exists involves a high degree of subjectivity and judgment and is based on the information available to management at a point in time.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At December&#160;31, 2013, we had two trust preferred securities with an aggregate amortized cost of $1.0 million and aggregate unrealized gain of $1.5 million.&#160; Both of these securities have fixed rates of interest and were placed back on accrual during 2012.&#160; The issuers of these securities are banks.  As of December&#160;31, 2013, through review of the current and expected cash flow analysis based on the credit quality of the underlying collateral, the class of securities we own, default probabilities and anticipated losses given default assumptions and stress tests performed on these securities, there was no other-than-temporary impairment loss taken for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Unrealized losses on other investments have not been recognized into income because the issuer(s)&#160;securities are of investment grade (except for Strats-Goldman Sachs Corporation as indicated below and three private placement collateralized mortgage obligations), management does not intend to sell and it is more likely than not that management would not be required to sell the securities prior to their anticipated recovery, and the decline in fair value is largely due to changes in interest rates.&#160; The fair value is expected to recover as the bond(s)&#160;approach maturity.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At December&#160;31, 2013, we had a $2.5 million Strats-Goldman Sachs Corporation obligation, maturing February&#160;15, 2034 which had been rated below investment grade but was no longer being rated as of December&#160;31, 2013.&#160; This is a variable rate note based on the six month LIBOR. The current rate on the security is 1.34%. The unrealized loss on this security was $1.1 million and $1.2 million as of December&#160;31, 2013 and December&#160;31, 2012 respectively.&#160; Strats-Goldman Sachs is paying as agreed.&#160; This loss has not been considered other-than-temporary in that we do not intend to sell the security and it is more likely than not that we will not be required to sell the security before the recovery of the cost basis, which may be at maturity.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">At December&#160;31, 2013, we had three private placement collateralized mortgage obligations totaling $1.2 million which are rated below investment grade.&#160; All were rated investment grade at the time of purchase.&#160; The net unrealized gain at December&#160;31, 2013 was $59,000.&#160; Through review of the current and expected cash flow analysis based on the credit quality of the underlying collateral, default probabilities and anticipated losses, two of these securities had been considered impaired and other-than-temporary impairment loss taken for the year ended December&#160;31, 2011 totaling $75,000.&#160; There was no other-than-temporary impairment loss taken for the year ended December&#160;31, 2013 or 2012.&#160; These securities remain available for sale as of December&#160;31, 2013.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Investment Securities.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, we had $169.0 million, or 22.8% of total assets, invested in investment securities, which consisted primarily of U.S. Government obligations, tax-exempt securities and corporate debt obligations.&#160; Investment securities increased $2.5 million or 1.5% at December&#160;31, 2013 as compared to December&#160;31, 2012.&#160; The increase in investment securities was primarily the result of an increase in municipal deposits requiring collateralization partially offset by the growth in net loans receivable.  </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">16</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s47e41702b5fd419890fc472c7a70ad17"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">We are required to designate securities as held to maturity, available for sale or trading, depending on our ability and intent regarding our investments.&#160; As of November 30, 2013, the Company transferred securities totaling $98.9 million with unrealized losses of $4.3 million from available for sale to held to the held to maturity portfolio.  These securities were transferred to help mitigate interest rate risk on the most price sensitive securities.  As a result, the securities are carried at fair value at the date of transfer, which established a new cost basis for book, and the difference between the par value of the securities and the fair at the date of transfer will be accreted as an adjustment of yield.  Investment securities in which the fair value option has been elected are considered trading assets and are recorded at fair value with changes in fair value included in earnings.&#160; style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;border-top:1px solid #000000;"><div style="font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">(1)</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:3pt;">&#160;&#160;</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;Weighted average yield has not been adjusted to reflect tax equivalent adjustments.</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td><td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td><td colspan="3" style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;padding-right:2px;"><div style="overflow:hidden;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Mortgage-Backed Securities</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;">.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; We purchase mortgage-backed securities in order to: (i)&#160;generate positive interest rate spreads with minimal administrative expense; (ii)&#160;lower our credit risk; and (iii)&#160;increase liquidity.&#160; At </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">, we had $99.0 million or 13.3% of total assets invested in mortgage-backed securities, of which $59.0 million were classified as held to maturity.&#160; The mortgage-backed securities portfolio had coupon rates ranging from 0.44% to 7.75%, a weighted average yield of 2.02% and a weighted average life (including payment assumption) of 5.72 years at </font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">December&#160;31, 2013</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Mortgage-backed securities are created by the pooling of mortgages and the issuance of a security with an interest rate that is less than the interest rate on the underlying mortgages.&#160; Mortgage-backed securities typically represent a participation interest in a pool of single-family or multi-family mortgages, although we focus our investments on mortgage-related securities backed by single-family mortgages. The issuers of such securities (generally U.S. Government agencies and government sponsored enterprises, including Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae) pool and resell the participation interests in the form of securities to investors, such as Oneida Savings Bank, and guarantee the payment of principal and interest to these investors. Mortgage-backed securities generally yield less than the loans that underlie such securities because of the cost of payment guarantees and credit enhancements. In addition, mortgage-related securities are usually more liquid than individual mortgage loans and may be used to collateralize certain of our liabilities and obligations. Investments in mortgage-backed securities involve a risk that actual prepayments will be greater than estimated over the life of the security, which may require adjustments to the amortization of any </font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">19</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="sff54cb466d384afe9e64966a363d4f37"></a><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">premium or accretion of any discount relating to such instruments thereby reducing the net yield on such securities. There is also reinvestment risk associated with the cash flows from such securities or in the event such securities are redeemed by the issuer. In addition, the market value of such securities may be adversely affected by changes in interest rates. Management reviews prepayment estimates periodically to ensure that prepayment assumptions are reasonable considering the underlying collateral for the securities at issue and current interest rates and to determine the yield and estimated maturity of our mortgage-backed securities portfolio. Of our $99.0 million mortgage-backed securities portfolio at December&#160;31, 2013, $3.0 million with a weighted average yield of 1.29% had contractual maturities within five years, $14.0 million with a weighted average yield of 2.99% had contractual maturities of five to ten years and $82.0 million with a weighted average yield of 2.36% had contractual maturities of over ten years. However, the actual maturity of a mortgage-backed security may be less than its stated maturity due to prepayments of the underlying mortgages or significant defaults of the underlying mortgages. Prepayments that are faster than anticipated may shorten the life of the security and may result in a loss of any premiums paid and thereby reduce the net yield on such securities. Although prepayments of underlying mortgages depend on many factors, the difference between the interest rates on the underlying mortgages and the prevailing mortgage interest rates generally is the most significant determinant of the rate of prepayments. Historically, during periods of declining mortgage interest rates, refinancing generally increases and accelerates the prepayment of the underlying mortgages and the related security. Under such circumstances, we may be subject to reinvestment risk because, to the extent that our mortgage related securities prepay faster than anticipated, we may not be able to reinvest the proceeds of such repayments and prepayments at a comparable rate of return.&#160; During 2013, mortgage interest rates began to increase coming off of historical low levels. The impact on our mortgage-backed securities portfolio is to decrease the prepayments slightly.&#160;Should interest rates continue to rise prepayments may decline, thereby extending the estimated life of the security and depriving us of the ability to reinvest cash flows at the increased rates of interest. </font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Collateralized Mortgage Obligations (&#8220;CMOs&#8221;) are debt securities issued by a special-purpose entity that aggregates pools of mortgages and mortgage-backed securities and creates different classes of securities with varying maturities and amortization schedules, as well as a residual interest, with each class possessing different risk characteristics.&#160; The cash flows from the underlying collateral are generally divided into &#8220;tranches&#8221; or classes that have descending priorities with respect to the distribution of principal and interest cash flows, while cash flows on pass-through mortgage-backed securities are distributed pro rata to all security holders.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">20</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><a name="s3b12f2aca84b4760b6f37763f1bb449a"></a><div><div style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:60px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Mortgage-Backed Securities.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; Set forth below is information relating to our mortgage-backed securities for the periods indicated.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font #000000;padding-left:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"><div style="text-align:right;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#8212;</font></div></td><td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:1px solid #000000;"><div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></td></tr></table></div></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><a name="s2551619FF19CDDFF45575CB22022752F"></a><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Trust Activities</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Oneida Savings Bank provides trust and investment services, acts as executor or administrator of estates and as trustee or custodian for various types of trusts.&#160; Trust services are offered through Oneida Savings Bank&#8217;s Trust Department.&#160; Services include fiduciary services for trusts and estates, money management and custodial services.&#160; At December&#160;31, 2013, Oneida Savings Bank maintained 530 trust/fiduciary accounts, with total assets of $186.8 million under management as compared to 477 trust/fiduciary accounts, with total assets of $112.9 million at December&#160;31, 2012.  Management anticipates that in the future the Trust Department will become a more significant component of Oneida Savings Bank&#8217;s business.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Personnel</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">As of December&#160;31, 2013, we had 337 full-time employees and 29 part-time employees.&#160; The employees are not represented by a collective bargaining unit.&#160; Management believes that we have a good relationship with its employees.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-weight:bold;">Regulation</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General.</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160; Oneida Savings Bank is a New York chartered savings bank and our deposit accounts are insured up to applicable limits by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation under the Deposit Insurance Fund.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank is subject to extensive regulation by the New York State Department of Financial Services (the &#8220;Department&#8221;) as its chartering agency, and by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, as the insurer of its deposit accounts.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank must file reports with the Department and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation concerning its activities and financial condition in addition to obtaining regulatory approvals prior to entering into certain transactions, including acquisitions of other financial institutions.&#160; Oneida Savings Bank is examined periodically by the Department and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation to test Oneida Savings Bank&#8217;s compliance with various laws and regulations.&#160; This regulation and supervision, as well as federal and state law, establishes a comprehensive framework of activities in which Oneida Savings Bank may engage and is intended primarily for the protection of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance fund and depositors.&#160; The regulatory structure also gives the regulatory authorities extensive discretion in connection with their supervisory and enforcement activities and with their examination policies, including policies with respect to the classification of assets and the establishment of adequate loan loss reserves for regulatory purposes.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Any change in these laws or regulations, whether by the Department or the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation could have a material adverse impact on Oneida Financial Corp. and Oneida Savings Bank and their operations.</font></div><br><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">24</font></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div></div><br><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">Set forth below is a brief description of certain regulatory requirements that are applicable to Oneida Financial Corp. and Oneida Savings Bank.&#160; The description below is limited to certain material aspects of the statutes and regulations addressed, and is not intended to be a complete description of such statutes and regulations and their effects on Oneida Financial Corp. and Oneida Savings Bank.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Dodd-Frank Act</font><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">.&#160; In 2010, Congress enacted the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (&#8220;Dodd-Frank Act&#8221;) which is significantly changing the bank regulatory structure and affecting the lending, investment, trading and operating activities of depository institutions and their holding companies.&#160; As of July&#160;21, 2011, the Dodd-Frank Act authorized the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System to supervise and regulate all savings and loan holding companies, like Oneida Financial Corp., in addition to bank holding companies which it currently regulates.&#160; The Office of Thrift Supervision, which was Oneida Financial Corp.&#8217;s prior regulator, was eliminated.&#160; The Dodd-Frank Act required the Federal Reserve Board to set minimum capital levels for bank and savings and loan holding companies that are as stringent as those required for the insured depository subsidiaries, and the components of Tier 1 capital would be restricted to capital instruments that are currently considered to be Tier 1 capital for insured depository institutions.&#160; Bank holding companies with assets of less than $500 million are exempt from these capital requirements.&#160; Under the Dodd-Frank Act, the proceeds of trust preferred securities will be excluded from Tier 1 capital unless such securities were issued prior to May&#160;19, 2010 by bank or savings and loan holding companies with less than $15 billion of assets.&#160; The legislation also established a floor for capital of insured depository institutions that cannot be lower than the standards in effect today, and directed the federal banking regulators to implement new leverage and capital requirements within 18 months that take into account off-balance sheet activities and other risks, including risks relating to securitized products and derivatives.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">&#160;</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The Dodd-Frank Act also created a new Consumer Financial Protection Bureau with broad powers to supervise and enforce consumer protection laws.&#160; The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has broad rule-making authority for a wide range of consumer protection laws that apply to all banks and savings institutions such as Oneida Savings Bank, including the authority to prohibit &#8220;unfair, deceptive or abusive&#8221; acts and practices.&#160; The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has examination and enforcement authority over all banks and savings institutions with more than $10 billion in assets.&#160; Banks and savings institutions with $10 billion or less in assets continue to be examined for compliance by their applicable bank regulators.&#160; The new legislation also weakened the federal preemption available for national banks and federal savings associations, and gave state attorney generals&#8217; the ability to enforce applicable federal consumer protection laws.</font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"><br></font></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;">The legislation broadened the base for Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance assessments.&#160;
